reader.requirement: At --std 85 a REWRITE of a sequential file executes only while the file is open in the I-O mode (opening I-O requires mass storage); never opened, closed, failed OPEN, INPUT, OUTPUT or EXTEND gives I-O status 49 (§1985:VII.1.3.5) with the record not replaced, the FROM move still made (GR4 a), and an applicable USE procedure run.

edition-consulted.switches: refuses REWRITE WITH LOCK / WITH NO LOCK at 85 (COBOL0900)
DialectBehavior.FileSharingFacility off at 85 for OPEN arbitration and locking; the 49 test does not consult it

reader.edition-search: grep CobolVersion|DialectBehavior|Edition in src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/IO; RewriteShared, RewriteRecord, MutationOpenModeGuard read; grep mass storage in src
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f20_02 covers I-O success and INPUT 49; not exercised: never opened, OUTPUT, EXTEND, after CLOSE, after a failed OPEN I-O, REWRITE FROM in a non-I-O mode, the USE procedure on 49; the mass-storage half has no non-mass-storage medium to probe (every sequential file is a disk file; a non-seekable stream answers through NotRewritableInPlace)

probes.printed: NOTOPEN=49 / OUTPUT=49 / CLOSED=49 / EXTEND=49 / INPUT-FROM=49 AREA=FROM / IO-FROM=00 / BACK=00 FROM / USE-G 35 OPENIO-G=35 / USE-G 49 REWRITE-G=49
probes.expected: 49 in every non-I-O state including after a failed OPEN I-O, USE runs; FROM move happens before the refused REWRITE; I-O REWRITE FROM replaces the record

probes.printed: COBOL0900 on REWRITE F-REC WITH NO LOCK (targeting COBOL-85)
probes.expected: the 2002 lock phrase is not in the 1985 REWRITE format

citations.check: OK  §1985:VII.4.5.4 GR1  (4.5.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR1
OK  §1985:VII.1.3.5  (1.3.5 I-O Status)  the text is in the clause; it lies in GRL2.4h

reader.notes: MutationOpenModeGuard is the one edition-free 49 test for REWRITE and DELETE of every organization, asked before the 43 gate, so a REWRITE in OUTPUT mode after a WRITE answers 49 (1985 lets the implementor choose when 43 and 49 both apply). The mass-storage requirement cannot be violated by a reachable file in this implementation.

refuter.evidence: r6rw.cob (refute-1985-124/r6rw-001, --std 85): OPEN I-O on a file open INPUT gives 41 and leaves it INPUT; REWRITE FROM then 49, the FROM move made (AREA=FROM), USE run; OPEN INPUT on a file open I-O gives 41 and leaves it I-O; REWRITE then 43 (the file IS open I-O, and the failed OPEN was the last input-output statement, §1985:VII.4.5.4 GR2), not 49; after the 1985-only CLOSE WITH LOCK REWRITE 49, OPEN I-O 38, REWRITE 49; an EXTERNAL connector opened I-O and READ in the caller is REWRITTEN 00 by another program describing it (read back SUBR), and 49 after CLOSE; a device file (ASSIGN TO NUL) answers OPEN I-O 35, so no non-mass-storage file reaches I-O mode and its REWRITE is 49. cite.py: OK  §1985:VII.4.5.4 GR1 (4.5.4 General Rules) the text is in GR1; OK  §1985:VII.1.3.5 ... GRL2.4h (49).
